_readme: Monthly Family History Challenge for the whole family. One object per month. id is YYYY-MM. title is the shared theme. kids, parents, and together each have a title and exactly three steps. link is optional and must be an https FamilySearch or Church page that loads. Owned by Sister Shalisa Bingham. Do not add a phone number or email.

kids.title: All About Me Box
steps: Find a box at home.
Put in three things that show who you are.
Tell a parent why you picked them.

parents.title: Add a Memory
steps: Sign in to Family Tree.
Open your own page or a parent's page.
Add one short memory in your own words.

together.title: Story Night
steps: Sit together for ten minutes.
Each person shares one thing from the box or one memory.
Thank the person who shared.

kids.title: One Fact from My Year
steps: With a parent, open the activity.
Pick one fact from the year you were born.
Tell someone at home what you found.
kids.linkLabel: Open The Year I Was Born

parents.title: Add a Birth Date
steps: Pick one person whose birth date or place is missing.
Add the date or place you know.
Read it back to be sure it is right.

together.title: A Year at Dinner
steps: Choose a parent or grandparent.
Find one fact from the year they were born.
Tell that fact at dinner.

kids.title: The Story of My Name
steps: Ask a parent how you got your name.
Ask if a relative shares that name.
Tell the story back in your own words.

parents.title: Index a Batch
steps: Open Indexing and sign in.
Choose one short batch.
Finish it so another family can find a name.

together.title: Say the Names
steps: Gather the family.
Say the names of parents and grandparents out loud.
Let each child say their own name and who they were named for.

kids.title: Where I'm From
steps: Name one place your family has lived.
Find that place on a map with a parent.
Say one thing you know about it.

parents.title: Add a Place
steps: Pick one person on the tree.
Add a birthplace or a place they lived.
Check the spelling with someone who knows.

together.title: Map Night
steps: Open a map together.
Point to one place your family is from.
Tell one story from that place.

kids.title: Interview a Grandparent
steps: Ask what they loved to do at your age.
Ask for one story from when they were young.
Ask what they hope you remember.

parents.title: Save the Story
steps: Write down what was said, in their words.
Add that short story to their page.
Read it back to the person you asked, if you can.

together.title: Ask Together
steps: Sit with a grandparent, or call them.
Let a child ask the three questions.
A parent writes while everyone listens.

kids.title: Share a Family Photo
steps: Pick one family photo.
Ask who is in the picture.
Tell one story the photo reminds you of.

parents.title: Keep the Photo with the Person
steps: Choose the person in that photo.
Add the photo, or a note about it, on their page.
Write one sentence about what the photo shows.

together.title: Pass the Photo
steps: Pass one photo around the room.
Each person says who they see.
Leave the photo where the family will see it this week.

kids.title: Compare Faces
steps: Find a photo of you and a photo of an older relative.
Name two things that look the same.
Show a parent what you noticed.

parents.title: Choose a Clear Portrait
steps: Pick one relative who needs a clearer photo.
Choose the best portrait you have.
Add it, or a note about it, on their page.

together.title: Side by Side
steps: Set the two photos next to each other.
Let each child say one thing that matches.
Tell the name of the older relative.

kids.title: Draw Where We're From
steps: Pick a place your family is from.
Draw yourself there.
Show the picture to your family.

parents.title: Write the Place Down
steps: Write the place name from the drawing.
Add one fact you know about that place.
Save the place on the family tree if it is missing.

together.title: Heritage Night
steps: Look at the drawing together.
Share one food, song, or story from that place.
Let a child tell what they drew.

kids.title: Find Three People
steps: With a parent, open the family tree.
Find you, a parent, and a grandparent.
Say one name out loud.

parents.title: Add One Missing Link
steps: Look for one parent or spouse line that is empty.
Add the person if you know the name.
Stop if you are not sure, and ask a relative.

together.title: Point to the Tree
steps: Sit so everyone can see the tree.
Let a child point to each person they found.
A parent tells one fact about one of them.

kids.title: Draw the Poster
steps: Draw you at the bottom of a page.
Add your parents, then your grandparents.
Color it and write a name if you know it.

parents.title: Check the Names
steps: Read each name on the poster.
Compare it with Family Tree.
Fix a spelling together if one is off.

together.title: Hang It Up
steps: Pick a wall the family walks past.
Hang the poster together.
Tell one story about someone on it.

kids.title: A Name and a Fact
steps: Ask a parent for one ancestor's name.
Learn one fact: a place, a job, or a story.
Tell that fact to someone at home.

parents.title: Attach a Source
steps: Open that ancestor on the tree.
Attach one record or note you already trust.
Read the fact back and see that it matches.

together.title: Family Home Evening
steps: Start with a song or a prayer, if you wish.
Let a child tell the ancestor's name and fact.
Close by saying thank you for that person.

kids.title: Write Your Own Story
steps: Pick one memory from this year.
Write three sentences or tell it out loud.
Save it with a parent.

parents.title: Write Your Story Too
steps: Pick one memory of your own.
Write a short paragraph.
Read it to your family.

together.title: Read Aloud
steps: Sit in a circle.
Each person reads or tells their story.
Clap for every story.

kids.title: Draw a Temple
steps: Draw a temple on paper.
Ask a parent one thing your family loves about the temple.
Put your picture up at home.

parents.title: Find a Family Name
steps: Open Ordinances Ready and sign in.
Find one family name you can prepare.
Save the name for a temple visit.

together.title: Plan the Visit
steps: Look at the child's temple drawing.
Pick a temple you can visit, even just the grounds.
Say the family name and why you want to go.
